newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends up on dlr supply, forwards steady.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends up on dlr supply, forwards steady.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended strongly against the dollar on Monday on good supply of the US currency and limited demand, dealers said.
They said the rupee ended at 35.81/82 per dollar against the day's opening quotes of 35.85/86 on a day marked by one-way movement in the exchange rate.
"The rupee was under no pressure at all today...only moving up," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There was little of the demand from east India which normally drags the rupee down."
He was referring to a large state-run bank based in eastern India whose actions normally determine the movement of the rupee-dollar rate.
Dealers said premia on forward dollars were steady in quiet trade on Monday.
"Rates hardly moved today," said a dealer. "Though the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was receiving premia, it was on a limited scale."
Dealers said the RBI rolled over December maturity swaps.
Premia for six-month dollars ended Monday at an annualised 7.54 percent against the weekend close of 7.48 percent.
